_comment: Manifest of free Windows diagnostic/repair tools for the fixit kit. 'license' is the real EULA category, not just 'is it $0' — a few well-known freeware tools restrict free use to personal/non-commercial, which matters since these PCs are being tested for resale. 'install' is 'winget' (scripted by install-tools.ps1) or 'manual' (documented URL, install by hand once).

tools.name: HWiNFO
tools.purpose: Deep hardware inventory + live sensors (temps, voltages, clocks, SMART) — first stop for 'what's actually in this PC and is it healthy'.
tools.licenseNote: Free for personal/home use per REALiX's EULA; commercial use (which testing PCs for resale may count as) technically requires a license. Prefer LibreHardwareMonitor or Sysinternals for anything you'd call business use.

tools.name: CPU-Z
tools.purpose: CPU/motherboard/RAM identification (exact model, timings, revision) — good for verifying what a listing actually contains.
tools.licenseNote: No personal/commercial distinction in CPUID's EULA.

tools.name: GPU-Z
tools.purpose: GPU identification + sensors, also reads VRAM health and BIOS version.

tools.name: LibreHardwareMonitor
tools.purpose: Open-source sensor monitor (temps/fans/voltages/clocks) — the commercial-use-safe alternative to HWiNFO/Speccy.

tools.name: CrystalDiskInfo
tools.purpose: SMART health/attributes for HDD/SSD/NVMe — catches failing drives before you build or sell on top of one.

tools.name: CrystalDiskMark
tools.purpose: Sequential/random read-write benchmark — confirms an SSD/NVMe is actually hitting its rated speed (e.g. not running at SATA speed in an NVMe slot, or a fake/counterfeit drive).

tools.name: WinDirStat
tools.purpose: Visual disk-space usage breakdown — find what's eating a drive.

tools.name: Rescuezilla
tools.purpose: Full-disk imaging/cloning (backup before risky repairs, or wipe-and-restore a known-good image). Bootable ISO, not an installed app.
tools.licenseNote: Named instead of Macrium Reflect Free, which Macrium discontinued for new users in 2023.

tools.name: MemTest86 (Free Edition)
tools.purpose: Bootable RAM stress test — the standard way to confirm or rule out bad memory as a crash cause.
tools.licenseNote: Free edition is free for any use; not reliably on winget, grab the ISO directly.

tools.name: Malwarebytes (Free)
tools.purpose: On-demand malware/PUP scan — free tier has no real-time protection, but scans and removes for free.
tools.licenseNote: Free consumer edition; if this ever becomes a for-profit repair shop rather than occasional resale prep, check Malwarebytes' business terms.

tools.name: AdwCleaner
tools.purpose: Removes adware/browser hijackers/PUPs that general AV often leaves behind.

tools.name: Farbar Recovery Scan Tool (FRST)
tools.purpose: Produces a deep system diagnostic log (startups, services, drivers, browser policy) for manual malware triage — the tool malware-removal forums standardize on.

tools.name: Windows Defender Offline
tools.purpose: Boots to a clean pre-OS environment to scan/remove rootkits that hide from a running Windows. Built into Windows, launch from Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Scan options.

tools.name: Display Driver Uninstaller (DDU)
tools.purpose: Fully wipes GPU drivers (leftover files/registry keys included) before a clean reinstall — fixes driver-corruption crashes normal uninstall can't.

tools.name: Snappy Driver Installer Origin (SDIO)
tools.purpose: Offline driver database + installer — bring a system with no network driver online, or bulk-update drivers on a machine you're refurbishing.

tools.name: Ventoy
tools.purpose: Multi-ISO bootable USB — drop MemTest86, a Windows install ISO, Rescuezilla, and more on one stick, boot any of them from a menu.

tools.name: Rufus
tools.purpose: Single bootable-USB creator for a Windows install ISO.

tools.name: Windows Media Creation Tool
tools.purpose: Official Microsoft tool to download a clean Windows 10/11 ISO or make an install USB directly.

tools.name: Sysinternals Process Explorer
tools.purpose: Advanced Task Manager replacement — see what a process is really doing, DLLs loaded, handles held.

tools.name: Sysinternals Autoruns
tools.purpose: Every autostart location in one view (services, scheduled tasks, startup folders, browser extensions) — the fast way to find what's slowing boot or persisting malware.

tools.name: Sysinternals TCPView
tools.purpose: Live view of every network connection and the process that owns it — useful when something's phoning home or hogging bandwidth.

tools.name: Sysinternals Process Monitor
tools.purpose: Real-time file/registry/process activity trace — for root-causing 'why does this app fail' when the error message is useless.

tools.name: 7-Zip
tools.purpose: Archive tool, also handy for extracting driver/tool packages that ship as self-extracting zips.

tools.name: Notepad++
tools.purpose: Read logs/config files comfortably.

tools.name: Git for Windows
tools.purpose: Provides git + a bash environment; some Claude Code features (version control awareness) expect git to be present.

tools.name: Windows Terminal
tools.purpose: Modern terminal host for PowerShell — nicer place to run Claude Code than legacy conhost.

tools.name: PowerShell 7
tools.purpose: Current cross-platform PowerShell; some winget/module behavior is smoother here than on the Windows-10-era 5.1 that ships in the box.

builtinDiagnostics._comment: Already on every Windows install, zero cost, use before reaching for third-party tools.

commands.purpose: Scans and repairs corrupted Windows system files. Run in an elevated PowerShell/cmd.
Checks the component store for corruption (fast, read-only).
Repairs component-store corruption found above. Needs internet or a Windows install-media source.
Checks and repairs a drive's file system and bad sectors. Requires a reboot if run against the boot volume.
Recent System event log — first place to look for a crash's actual error/event ID.
Opens Reliability Monitor — a timeline of crashes/installs/failures, often the fastest way to correlate 'when did this start'.
Windows Memory Diagnostic — built-in RAM test, schedules a reboot-time scan (less thorough than MemTest86 but zero-install).
